items.title: Can Morality Be Binding Without Objective Justification? | Michael Ruse
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*Why do moral obligations feel absolute if they emerged through evolution?*

Michael Ruse explains how cooperation, reciprocal altruism, and kin selection may have shaped human morality. He then explores why moral obligations can remain deeply binding even if their authority comes from evolved psychology rather than an independent moral reality.

0:00 Altruism as a Biological Adaptation
2:07 Reciprocal Altruism, Kin Selection, and Their Limits 
5:40 Moral Obligations and Prescriptive Ethics 
6:59 Metaethics and Morality as an Adaptation 
9:21 Absolute Morality Without Objective Foundations

*Michael Ruse* (1940–2024) was a leading philosopher of biology known for his foundational work on evolutionary theory, ethics, the creation–evolution controversy, and the relationship between science and religion.

items.title: Ancient Hindu Cosmology and Modern Science | Swami Sarvapriyananda
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*How did ancient Hindu thinkers imagine cosmic timescales stretching across billions of years?*

Swami Sarvapriyananda explains why Hindu philosophy generally accommodates biological evolution and explores ancient ideas of recurring universes, fourteen worlds, and immense cosmic cycles. He considers their intriguing parallels with modern cosmology while emphasizing that these traditions were philosophical and imaginative rather than demonstrably scientific.

2:29 Evolution and Cycles of the Universe
4:30 Ancient Cosmology and Modern Scientific Parallels
6:06 Fourteen Worlds and Cosmic Timescales

*Swami Sarvapriyananda* is a Hindu monk of the Ramakrishna Order and head of the Vedanta Society of New York. He is a prominent teacher of Vedanta and has spoken internationally on Hindu philosophy, spirituality, and interfaith dialogue.

items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:

Paul Allen explores Ernan McMullin's approach to scientific realism, including how scientists infer causes from observable effects without claiming deductive certainty. items.title: How Consciousness Challenges Our Picture of the Cosmos | Thomas Nagel
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*What if the mind-body problem reaches far beyond the human brain?*

Thomas Nagel traces how his thinking about subjective experience developed into a broader challenge to materialist explanations of nature. He discusses consciousness, reason, value, and the possibility of non-theistic teleology, while acknowledging that we do not yet know what a comprehensive alternative theory would look like.

2:54 Realism About Experience, Reason, and Value 
5:19 The Mind-Body Problem as a Cosmological Problem

*Thomas Nagel* is an American philosopher and Professor of Philosophy and Law at New York University. His work focuses on philosophy of mind, ethics, and political philosophy, and he is especially known for his influential critique of reductionist accounts of consciousness.

items.title: Are We Getting Closer To Truth? | Robert Lawrence Kuhn, Interviewed by Àlex Gómez-Marín
items.author: Closer To Truth
items.content:
<article>*In a first for _Closer To Truth,_ the roles are reversed: Àlex Gómez-Marín interviews Robert Lawrence Kuhn, the creator and host of the series.*

Can understanding a question more deeply be satisfying even without an answer? Àlex Gómez-Marín asks Kuhn to reflect on the origins and purpose of _Closer To Truth._ Dr. Kuhn explains why understanding questions more deeply, encountering diverse perspectives, and connecting people across cultures can matter even when the ultimate answers remain unknown.

0:00 How Closer To Truth Got Its Name
1:40 Loving the Questions Without Final Answers
4:17 How Ultimate Questions Unite People
5:37 Bringing Beauty to the Search for Truth

*Robert Lawrence Kuhn* is the creator, executive producer, writer, and host of _Closer To Truth,_ which has featured more than 500 leading scientists, philosophers, and creative thinkers in more than 5,000 videos and more than 350 public television episodes on PBS stations. He holds a PhD in anatomy/neuroscience from the UCLA Brain Research Institute and an MBA from MIT's Sloan School of Management. He is the author or editor of more than 30 books, including _The Mystery of Existence: Why Is There Anything At All?_ (with John Leslie), and the author of the Landscape of Consciousness, a taxonomy of more than 500 theories of consciousness.

*Àlex Gómez-Marín* is a Spanish physicist turned neuroscientist. He holds a PhD in theoretical physics and a Masters in biophysics from the University of Barcelona. He was a research fellow at the EMBL-CRG Centre for Genomic Regulation and at the Champalimaud Centre for the Unknown in Lisbon. His research spans from the origins of the arrow of time in inert systems, to the neurobiology of action-perception in living organisms such as flies, worms, mice, and humans.
